findings.passage: In Pennsylvania, the only time you need to show ID to vote is the first time. This is despite overwhelming public support for implementing voter ID every time you go to the polls.
findings.note: Op-ed by Klunk dated 9/23/2024 on the House caucus site: notes ID is now required only for a first-time voter and says voter ID should apply every time.

findings.passage: Despite bipartisan support, partisan operating rules in the House have halted progress on voter ID, preventing Pennsylvania voters from having the final say on the matter.
findings.note: Same op-ed: says House operating rules have stopped progress on voter ID.

findings.passage: A voter identification constitutional amendment, House Bill 891, has sat idle in the House State Government Committee for over a year. House Republicans launched a discharge petition in March as an attempt to advance the measure, but it has not yet moved. Under the rules of the House, discharge petitions require the signatures of at least 25 Democrats and 25 Republicans to be successful. I am proud to be one of the signatures on that petition, but time is running out.
findings.note: Same op-ed: says she signed the discharge petition to move HB 891, a voter ID constitutional amendment.

findings.passage: Election integrity is fundamental for the proper functioning of democracy. By implementing robust verification processes, and working toward other goals like addressing system failures, and fostering community engagement, we can prevent fraud, safeguard legitimate votes, and uphold public trust in our institutions.
findings.note: Same op-ed: general statement on election integrity and verification.
